metaDescription: Own minerals under farmland near West Liberty, WV? We trace the Ohio County deed record, check any old lease, and buy fractional or whole interests.
heroLead: West Liberty grew up around its farmland and its university, and the mineral estate under most of that farmland was severed and leased generations before the campus was even built.
intro: Ohio County's northern panhandle farmland has a long, quiet production history — shallow gas wells drilled on family tracts around West Liberty going back well before the modern Marcellus and Utica boom reshaped drilling economics further south and east. The deeds recording those old severances are still the controlling document for who owns the mineral estate under a given West Liberty parcel today.

We start every file the same way: pulling the Ohio County record to trace the mineral chain, checking whether an old lease is still attached to the tract, and identifying every heir with a claim to it before we put a number on the table.

sections.heading: Ohio County's Farm-Tract Legacy
paragraphs: Much of the land around West Liberty was farmed for generations before being divided among heirs, sold in pieces, or partly developed. The mineral rights under those tracts often followed a separate path from the surface, reserved out in a deed when a farm was sold, or split unevenly when an estate passed to multiple children.
That means the person paying the property tax bill on a West Liberty lot today isn't always the person who owns what's underneath it, and sorting that out is usually the first real step in a sale.

sections.heading: Where West Liberty Sits on the Play
paragraphs: West Liberty sits on the flank rather than the core of the Marcellus and Utica fairway, closer in character to the legacy Gordon Sand and Big Injun production that defined this part of Ohio County for most of the twentieth century than to the dense modern pad development further south in Marshall and Wetzel Counties.

That doesn't make a West Liberty interest worthless — legacy production and future drilling potential both factor into what we're willing to pay — but it does change how we approach valuation compared to a tract sitting in the middle of active lateral development.

sections.heading: Old Leases, New Royalty Checks
paragraphs: Some of the leases still on file against West Liberty tracts are flat-rate agreements from decades ago, paying a fixed annual amount that has nothing to do with current gas prices or production volume. If a lease like that falls short of West Virginia's 1/8 statutory royalty floor and there's active or planned drilling nearby, it may be entitled to convert to a royalty-paying structure.

We check the lease terms and well status on every tract before we make an offer, because the difference between a flat-rate lease and a properly converted one changes what the underlying interest is worth.

sections.heading: Splitting an Estate in Ohio County
paragraphs: It's common for a West Liberty mineral interest to be held today by several siblings or cousins, each owning an undivided fraction inherited from a grandparent's farm and never formally divided among them. That kind of ownership doesn't need to be untangled before you sell your share.
We buy individual fractional interests directly from a single heir, and we handle the deed and closing paperwork so you're not the one chasing down relatives to sign off.

faqs.question: How do I know if my family's mineral rights near West Liberty were ever leased?
faqs.answer: We check the Ohio County record for any recorded lease or memorandum of lease tied to your specific parcel and tell you what's on file before you decide anything.

faqs.question: My interest is a small fraction inherited from my grandparents. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes, small undivided fractional interests are common in this part of Ohio County and we buy them regularly, one heir at a time if needed.

faqs.question: Is West Liberty in an active drilling area right now?
faqs.answer: It sits closer to the flank of the play than the drilling core further south, so activity is less concentrated, but that's part of what we factor into an offer, not a reason an interest has no value.
